mahjongcraft.rule_catalogue.riichi.entry: A triplet or quad of the prevailing wind.
Win by robbing another player's added kan.
Every group and the pair contains a terminal or honor.
A non-dealer wins on their first draw without any intervening calls.
A hand containing tiles of one suit only.
A hand made entirely of terminals.
A hand made of seven distinct pairs.
A triplet or quad of white, green, or red dragons.
A closed 1112345678999 shape in one suit plus one tile of that suit; nine-sided wait is true Nine Gates.
Ron on the last discard, and the tile is the nine of dots. Counted instead of Under the River.
A closed hand of two each of the 2 to 8 of bamboo.
Seven pairs made of one pair each of all seven honor tiles. All Honors is not counted on top.
Triplets or quads of all three dragons.
A closed hand of two each of the 2 to 8 of dots.
Triplets or quads of all four winds.
A closed hand of two each of the 2 to 8 of characters.

The next tile after an indicator is dora: a four-character indicator makes five characters dora. Each copy adds one han but is not a yaku. Extra indicators revealed after kan count kan dora in the same way.
Riichi declared on the first uninterrupted discard turn.
Tsumo on the last live-wall tile; a closed hand is not required.
One suit together with honors.
A hand made only of terminals and honors.
Ron on the last live-wall discard; a closed hand is not required.
Win by tsumo on the last live-wall draw, and the tile is the one of dots. Counted instead of Under the Sea.
123, 456, and 789 in one suit.
Two identical sequences in a closed hand.
Win within one uninterrupted turn after riichi.
After a double riichi, win on the last live-wall draw or the last discard.
Three identical sequences in one suit, such as three sets of 123 characters. Counted instead of Pure Double Sequence.
A triplet or quad of the player's seat wind.
Every group and the pair contains a terminal, with no honors.
Nine gates with all nine tile waits in one suit.
Ron on the tile another player discards right after a kan and its replacement draw.
One of each thirteen distinct terminal and honor types, with one type repeated as the pair.
Thirteen orphans with thirteen-sided wait.
Before the first discard and without a call, the initial hand contains nine or more distinct terminal and honor types.
At exhaustive draw, a non-empty discard pond contains only terminals and honors and no discard was claimed.

In three-player mahjong you may set a North aside after drawing and take a replacement tile. Each North set aside adds one han but is not a yaku, and it also counts toward dora and ura dora. It is not a discard, but other players may ron on it.
Four sequences, a valueless pair, and a two-sided wait in a closed hand.
Riichi declared with a closed tenpai hand.
Each red five adds one han but is not a yaku. A red five may also count as visible dora.
A non-dealer wins by ron before their own first draw, with no calls in between.
Tsumo on a rinshan tile after kan.
Two pairs of identical sequences in a closed hand.
A hand using only 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 bamboo and green dragons.
Three concealed triplets or quads.
Three declared kans.
Three triplets (or kans) of consecutive numbers in one suit, such as 333, 444 and 555 characters.
The same sequence in all three suits.
The same triplet in all three suits.
All four sets are called with chi, pon or open kan and you win on a single-tile wait. A closed kan breaks it.
Two dragon triplets and a pair of the third dragon.
Three wind triplets and a pair of the fourth wind.
Four concealed triplets or quads.
Four concealed triplets with a single-tile wait.
Four declared kans.
All four players have declared riichi and the required discard window resolves.
All four players discard the same wind first, without a call or other interruption.
Four kans are declared by different players in total; four kans by one player do not qualify, and the required discard resolves without ron.
A hand containing no terminals or honors.
The dealer wins by tsumo before the first discard.
A hand made entirely of triplets or quads.
Ron on the tile another player discarded to declare riichi.
A hand made entirely of honors.
Win by self-draw with a closed hand.

After a riichi win, count dora using the hidden indicators beneath the visible ones. Each copy adds one han but is not a yaku. Kan ura dora uses the hidden indicators beneath the added kan indicators.
The winning hand uses characters, dots, bamboo, winds and dragons. Seven pairs also counts.
mahjongcraft.rule_catalogue.riichi.examp: Dora only add han when the hand already has a yaku.
Win by robbing another player's added kan.
A non-dealer wins on their first self-draw before any calls.
Ron with the nine of dots on the last discard.
Declared on the first uninterrupted discard turn.
Win by tsumo on the last live-wall draw.
Win by ron on the last live-wall discard.
Win by tsumo with the one of dots on the last live-wall draw.
Win within one uninterrupted turn after riichi.
After a double riichi, win by tsumo on the last live-wall draw.
Ron on the tile another player discards after a kan.
Two Norths set aside add two han.
A non-dealer wins by ron before their own first draw, with no calls.
Win after declaring riichi.
Win by tsumo on a rinshan draw after kan.
Win on another player's discard.
The prevailing wind is west.
The player's seat wind is west.
The dealer wins by tsumo before the first discard.
Ron on another player's riichi declaration tile.
Win by self-draw with a closed hand.
mahjongcraft.rule_catalogue.riichi.label: Not a yaku
Only adds han when the hand already has a yaku. It cannot win on its own.
Closed hand only
Not valid after any chi, pon or open kan.
Double yakuman
1 han
2 han
3 han
5 han
6 han
Local yaku
An old yaku most rule sets no longer use. It only counts when local yaku are turned on in the rule settings.
Mangan
Worth one han less after any chi, pon or open kan.
1 han open
2 han open
5 han open
Yakuman
Nine terminals and honors abortive draw
